route-instructions.task: On an actual safe floor/table grid, place a start square, a toy destination and a removable obstacle. Learner gives then follows an own step-by-step route using forward/turn and beside/behind/near language. A partner follows it literally. Test an original mistaken route (forward2 when3 are needed), locate the mismatching step and revise; record the working sequence with actual arrows, words or pictures. Change the obstacle and start to require a new route, not a memorised recital.
route-instructions.positive: Creation AND following, actual test/repair and a recoverable record all occur.
route-instructions.nearMiss: Copies a route picture without giving directions, repairs by moving the destination, or calls an untested sequence correct.
route-instructions.transfer: Changed start/obstacle forces a newly tested recorded sequence.
route-instructions.wholeClaimBoundary: Retain the existing instruction claim’s everyday-task, missing-step prediction and exact computer-following checks. Introduce one actual computer example; the existing diverse-device recognition prerequisite remains separate. The route includes left/right and position descriptions; quarter/half/whole turns are additional whole-card checks, not newly invented mandatory K vocabulary.

inquiry-build-test.task: Offer actual safe foil/card/plastic materials and a shallow supervised water tray. Learner poses a question about a small boat/model carrying large counters, predicts before testing, selects appropriate materials/tools, builds it and records observations as counters are added in a consistent stated way. Keep design purpose/criterion explicit. Compare a revised design with the first, state an evidence-supported conclusion and communicate the result through an own drawing/oral account/data record. An observation investigation need not be falsely called a controlled experiment; a deliberate controlled comparison keeps the stated changed factor and relevant conditions consistent. Repeat with a changed material/criterion. Actually build and test both prepared model cases. Across these investigations and the environment task, generate at least three genuine how/why questions and choose among observation, a test and an adult-supported reference enquiry. Record the first prediction before any trial. Compare an own result to that prediction, communicate the evidence, propose a changed-case prediction and one concrete method improvement.
inquiry-build-test.positive: Own question/prediction, justified selection, actual construction/testing/observation, evidence-supported conclusion and communicated result are present.
inquiry-build-test.nearMiss: Shows a finished adult model, invents observations, changes several factors while attributing an effect to one, or treats the initial prediction as a law.
inquiry-build-test.transfer: Changed model/material/criterion requires a fresh prediction, test and explanation.
inquiry-build-test.limits: A child prediction that heavier things sink faster is something to investigate, not a physics law. No testing of children, animals, food, fire or hazardous substances.
inquiry-build-test.wholeClaimBoundary: Retain the whole existing modelling, equipment observation, recording and conclusion claims, including a changed case. Existing hard prerequisites remain; association never certifies that readiness. Table/bar-chart/key readiness for the broader inherited data-presentation path remains separately assessed, rather than falsely becoming an Ontario K obligation.

safety-and-get-help.task: Before the actual build/movement activities identify a safe work area and applicable classroom rules, demonstrate safe handling, and explain what injury a chosen rule helps prevent. Use an original fictional card: a pupil has a collision and says their head hurts or they do not feel right. Choose to stop the activity and tell a trusted adult for help; no child diagnoses a concussion or decides return-to-play. Separately use offline fictional in-person/online discomfort cards (a person asks for an address or a game feels unsafe): pause/stop, avoid sharing private information and seek a suitable trusted adult. Change the setting and identify another help route if the first adult is unavailable.
safety-and-get-help.positive: Actual safe practice, a reason for the rule and age-appropriate help-seeking in both in-person/online cases are demonstrated.
safety-and-get-help.nearMiss: Recites a rule while handling equipment unsafely, keeps playing through a suspected injury, or shares personal information to make an unfamiliar online person happy.
safety-and-get-help.transfer: Different activity/contact context requires a suitable safe action and help route.
safety-and-get-help.limits: Fictional scenarios only; no actual injury demonstration, clinical assessment, recovery timetable, compulsory trauma disclosure or real stranger contact.

natural-built-investigation.task: Compare an actual supervised local planted patch and a built paved/covered area using questions, observations or appropriately dated attributed records. Ask about and describe a natural occurrence, such as a plant change or puddle after rain, without inventing an observed cause. Sort a small actual/photo set containing a living plant/animal and a rock/toy by living/non-living, explaining evidence and a near miss (a battery toy moves but is not alive; a dormant seed need not visibly grow now). Compare actual repeating/similar forms in the two environments while distinguishing approximate natural patterns from perfect repeated tiles; do not claim all nature follows an ABB rule. Use a hand lens or other suitable simple equipment to describe and compare actual observable features. Include a plant, a fallen dead leaf, a stone and a battery toy so the separate whole living/dead/never-alive claim can be checked without mistaking movement for life. For the whole local-feature claim at age six, separately distinguish an actual natural feature, a managed planted area and a built feature, locating their relative positions on a simple prepared/own plan. The source task itself does not require the full older classification vocabulary or claim that all environments are untouched nature.
natural-built-investigation.positive: Own question/description, supported classification and a comparison of patterns in natural ANDbuilt settings occur.
natural-built-investigation.nearMiss: Uses movement alone as a definition of life, calls a dormant seed dead merely because it is still, or describes only the human-made location.
natural-built-investigation.transfer: New item or observation tests the classification/comparison; use new actual environmental evidence.
natural-built-investigation.resourceCondition: Actual local environments or dated records must be selected; an invented universal local landscape is not substituted.
natural-built-investigation.wholeClaimBoundary: An equipment observation supports a specific pattern comparison; it does not establish that every natural shape has a formal repeating unit. Preserve dormant-seed and moving-toy counterexamples. The broader three-way life-history and natural/managed/built claims use a conservative single-age-six context, without lowering their whole-claim scope to four.

materials: two equal pieces of safe foil
build: Choose and shape a model intended to carry counters on water. Explain an intended shape/function relation.
Select a change to the hull shape while keeping foil amount and counter type the same.
test: Before each trial predict what will happen. Add counters by the same stated method until the chosen stopping criterion is reached; do not invent results.
Compare actual first/revised designs, identifying what changed and what the results can support.
record: Draw the model and record actual counts/observations in a small table or supported tally.
Explain the result against the original question, compare the prediction and suggest one targeted improvement.
foil-boat.limits: Adult prepares safe materials, catches spills and supervises; no testing of a real boat carrying people or floating children.

build: Set a small gap and an intended load criterion. Choose, fold and join a simple spanning structure.
Compare an initial flat span with an own altered fold, retaining the same gap and stated load method.
test: Predict before loading, then test the actual constructed span by the same safe placement method.
Observe whether the stated criterion is met and compare the two versions with the actual evidence.
record: Draw the actual structure and its changed feature. Record the real outcome and explain why a supported shape choice mattered.
Give a changed-gap or changed-material prediction as a proposal, not an already measured result.
paper-bridge.limits: Small tabletop models only; no standing on a structure, sharp tools or high loads.
